p16: 16.  By a letter of 11 October 2001, the applicant asked the Ministry of Culture whether the copies of the book had been seized.
p17: 17.  On 17 October 2001 the head of the publications unit of the Ministry of Culture informed the applicant that the Ministry’s Publications Advisory Board, composed of seven professors, had considered that the book was a work of scientific research and that it did not contain any insults or expressions that could be regarded as insults. The applicant was also informed that the author of the book did not accept any amendments to the text and that, at his request, the Ministry had transferred the copyright in the book back to him.
p18: 18.  On 4 February 2002 the applicant wrote to the Ministry of Culture and to Associate Professor Ali Rafet Özkan, reiterating his initial request. He did not receive a reply.
p19: 19.  Subsequently, on 30 April 2002, the applicant, in his own name, brought proceedings in the Ankara Civil Court of First Instance (*tribunal de grande instance d’Ankara*) against the Ministry of Culture and the author of the book in question, seeking compensation for the non-pecuniary damage he claimed to have sustained as a result of the expressions contained in the book, which in his view constituted an attack on his Gypsy/Roma identity and were insulting. He also requested the confiscation of the copies of the book and a ban on its publication and distribution.
p20: 20.  The author replied that, in writing the book, he had made use of data obtained from the Adana police headquarters and of books written by other authors about Gypsies, and that he had had no intention of insulting or humiliating that community. He further stated that the passages to which the applicant referred should not be considered in isolation but in the light of the book as a whole.
p21: 21.  On 24 September 2002 the Ankara Civil Court of First Instance (*tribunal de grande instance d’Ankara*) dismissed the applicant’s claims in so far as they concerned the author of the book. It held that the book was the result of academic research, was based on scientific data and dealt with the social structures of Roma/Gypsies in Turkey. The court therefore concluded that the expressions in question did not insult the applicant. As to the applicant’s complaints against the Ministry, the court declared that it lacked jurisdiction to examine them and held that they fell within the jurisdiction of the administrative courts.
p22: 22.  On 25 October 2002 the applicant appealed against that decision, arguing that the book could not be regarded as a work of scientific research and that the Ministry of Culture should therefore not have published it.
p23: 23.  On 21 April 2003 the Court of Cassation (*Cour de cassation*) upheld the first-instance judgment. In its decision it stated that the impugned expressions were of a general nature and that there was therefore nothing to lead it to conclude that they concerned all Roma/Gypsies or that they constituted an attack on the applicant’s identity.
p24: 24.  On 8 December 2003 a request by the applicant for rectification of the decision was rejected.
p25: 25.  Subsequently, on an unspecified date, the applicant brought an action against the Ministry of Culture in the Ankara Administrative Court (*tribunal administratif d’Ankara*), seeking compensation for non-pecuniary damage and alleging that the content of the book published by the Ministry of Culture was offensive and insulting to the Roma/Gypsy community. On 7 April 2004 his claim was dismissed. The Administrative Court found that, before its publication, the book in question had been examined and approved by a rapporteur appointed by the Publications Advisory Board, which had then endorsed its publication. It noted that, following the applicant’s allegations, the Advisory Board, composed of seven professors, had re-examined the book on 25 September 2001 and had decided that it was an academic study based on scientific research and that its continued distribution and sale would not cause any harm. The Administrative Court therefore concluded that the applicant’s allegations were unfounded. The applicant did not appeal against that decision.
